extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard officers, government contracting officials, and public administration researchers
extracted.subtask_description: A master's thesis analyzing implementation of OMB Circular A-76 in the U.S. Coast Guard: how A-76 is implemented, causes of contract cost increases after award, comparisons with the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO), and perceptions of A-76 by USCG personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Commercial Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Government agencies must identify their 'commercial activities' that could be contracted out (with certain exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies develop an inventory of commercial activities which are reviewed for A-76 consideration and then reviewed by OMB for approval; responses to guidance may vary in specificity and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a Performance Work Statement (PWS) — a Statement of Work describing what the function is and what it takes to do it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PWS is the basis for solicitation and should include specifications and a Quality Assurance (QA) plan; it may be developed before or during the MEO determination and is used in the solicitation to offer the activity in competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a Quality Assurance (QA) Plan in the PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a QA plan within the PWS to ensure goods and services received meet the requirements of the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QA plan describes government actions to assure contractor performance; the thesis flags limited training/experience of COTRs as a common implementation problem affecting quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop the Government Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the PWS, determine the best organizational structure and operating procedures for performing the function in-house — the Most Efficient Organization (MEO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The MEO should encourage efficiency by 'cutting the fat' and is costed to provide the government in-house baseline for comparison with private offers; the 1979 revision emphasized measurable work standards (what is done) rather than how it's done.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-depth management study to determine MEO and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct an in-depth management study (including PWS and MEO costing) to determine the in-house cost baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective studies require advanced planning, preparation, skill, comprehensive analysis, and can be lengthy and burdensome; inaccurate studies are a documented problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed-bid confidentiality and bid-opening comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the Invitation for Bid (IFB/sealed bid) method, maintain confidentiality of cost data so government and contractor costs remain independent; the contracting officer does not know the in‑house cost estimate until bid opening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At bid opening the offeror and MEO costs are compared; sealed bid is used when contracts can be competed primarily on price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting-out decision 10% rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If total cost of contracting out is less than the MEO’s cost by more than 10 percent of the MEO’s personnel-related costs, and the offeror is determined responsible, then the commercial activity is contracted out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the offeror's cost is within 10% of the MEO cost or greater than the MEO, the activity remains in-house. Contractor responsibility is a required determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold rule for small functions (<10 FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: For functions having less than 10 full-time equivalents (FTE), a formal cost comparison is not required as long as the price is 'fair & reasonable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fair & reasonable is determined by presence of a number of firms in the service industry to induce competition; this exempts many small functions from full A-76 cost comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation term guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Bids or proposals should cover at least three years for multi-year funding, or cover two fiscal years after the initial year for single-year funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the typical contract funding basis used in A-76 solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sealed bid (IFB) vs RFP/negotiation and set-asides
rubrics_metrics.description: Most A-76 solicitations use IFB/sealed bid because many service contracts can be competed on price; some solicitations may be RFP/negotiated depending on type of work or if set-aside for small/disadvantaged firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set-asides (e.g., SBA Section 8(a)) may obviate cost comparisons and can influence competition and results (e.g., easier contracting-out when reserved for 8(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Return-to-in-house criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To return a contracted-out function to in-house, the MEO must better a private-sector offeror by a specified cost margin and the agency Secretary must approve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis states the MEO would have to better a private offeror by a ten percent cost increment (described as twenty percent lower than the originally competed MEO cost) plus 25% of the contractor’s capital assets cost; Secretary approval is required. Recompete reasons include unsatisfactory service or contract costs becoming unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for recompete/review
rubrics_metrics.description: Two primary reasons to recompete or conduct another cost comparison are (1) unsatisfactory service and (2) contract costs becoming unreasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, returning work to government control is difficult and rare; two USCG examples that returned in-house involved contractor default (safety-critical service) and persistent poor performance/cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reporting and timetable obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must develop inventories of commercial activities, review them for A-76 consideration, and report progress to OMB on timetables as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EO 12615 also required agencies to conduct annual studies of not less than 3% of civilian workforce until all potential commercial activities reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories defining 'commercial activities'
rubrics_metrics.description: A-76 provides a list of services considered 'commercial activities' (examples include: audiovisual, ADP services, food services, health services, industrial shops, maintenance/repair, printing, security, transportation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is illustrative, not exhaustive; correct classification affects whether an activity is subject to A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of measurable work standards in PWS/MEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Define needs for a commercial activity by measurable work standards (what is to be done), not by prescribing how the activity is performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This management concept (emphasized in the 1979 revision) supports fair competition by focusing on outcomes and performance requirements rather than methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration and quality oversight roles (COTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign Contracting Officer's Technical Representatives (COTRs) to monitor contractor performance; these personnel need adequate training and experience in quality assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The thesis cites the short duration (2–3 years) and limited training/experience of many COTRs as an implementation weakness; effective QA depends on capable COTRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of labor cost changes (DOL wage determinations) and added work as causes of cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations and added work as common causes of contract cost increases after award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous USCG studies found DOL wage determinations and added work caused cost increases though contracts could remain cost-effective; thesis updates and expands these findings to more activities and analyzes other contributing factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality to ensure independent cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain confidentiality of cost data to ensure Government and contractor cost estimates remain independent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality is especially important in sealed-bid processes; it preserves integrity of the cost comparison and prevents collusion or benchmarking against the MEO before bids are opened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized procedures and transmittal notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow OMB transmittal notices and the 1983 A-76 supplement which provide standardized procedures and changes in cost calculations for implementing A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay current with transmittals and executive orders (e.g., EO 12615) since they can change implementation requirements such as study rates or cost computation methods.
